Having compared them, I prefer being able to delete from any bookmark directly — the version A rule.

The archive-first version is certainly cautious, and I understand the thinking. But making me archive something *before* I'm allowed to delete it feels like an extra hoop for the times I already know, right now, that I want a link gone for good — a bit of junk I pasted by mistake, say. Forcing it to take a detour through the archive first is friction I don't want, and it slightly muddies the two ideas I liked keeping separate: archive is "set aside," not "the waiting room before the bin."

The confirmation warning is the safety net that matters to me — that pause where it names the bookmark and says this can't be undone is what stops accidents. As long as that's always there, I'm comfortable deleting straight from any card's menu. So: let me delete from anywhere, with the clear confirmation every time. That's version A.
